text:
maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout I see a new host-side 95th spike on tokenized requests. Started at ~16:20 UTC. Anyone else seeing this?

samir: Yep saw it on our internal canary. P95 +120ms on small chat requests (~30-200 tokens). Latency waterfall points to parsing/tokenization stage on host.

maya: Profiled a couple traces, looks like a lot of tiny writev calls from ingress -> proxy and repeated proto unmarshalling. KV cache hit-rate also dipped slightly. Paste from a sample flame (zoomed on host parse):
```
parse_request 65%
  tokenization 40%
    utf8-normalize 12%
    simple-tokenize 20%
    kv-lookup 8%
  serialize -> grpc-writev 15%
  allocs 10%
```

alicia: Interesting — KV hit-rate drop aligns with the new kernel hinting we rolled last week. We changed chunk boundaries which may be fragmenting cached prefixes. Hit-rate went from 87% -> 78% on the canary host.

jon: So two vectors: more small I/O and worse KV reuse. Could be the kernel selector's minibatch sizing creating shorter prefix windows.

ryan: Quick repro: run the e2e canary with heavy small-request mix (1000 qps, 70% small). I instrumented ingress with `tcpdump -w` and saw many 200-400B frames. HTTP2 HPACK overhead also visible.

samir: Proposed triage steps:
• revert kernel hint change on a single shard and compare p95
• increase ingress coalesce window from 150us -> 500us behind a feature flag to see writev reduction
• add a short-lived prefix-merging pass in preparse to try to preserve KV cache keys

maya: +1. Any estimate for perf delta from coalescing?

samir: From local microbench: coalesce window 150->500us reduced number of writev syscalls by ~3x and lowered parse CPU by ~9% on small reqs. End-to-end p95 improvement ~70-90ms in the smoke test.

alicia: For KV behavior: if chunk boundaries changed we can add a heuristic to keep last N tokens as a single key for caching (N=8) to avoid splitting common prefixes. Low risk A/B.

jon: Also check batching heuristic — if kernel selector is preferring tiny minibatches, we should bias towards slightly larger batches for small-sequence workloads. That will help amortize tokenize+serialize costs.

maya: I pushed a minimal feature-flag PR to try the coalesce change on canary: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingress/pulls/4321

ci-bot: Build passed — tests: unit 1200/1200, integration 87/87. Canary deploy plan: shard s-17.

ryan: Running canary now on s-17 with coalesce=500us + kernel-hint revert. Initial numbers (1 minute in): p95 back down ~60ms vs bad canary, KV hit-rate recovering to 84%.

maya: Nice. Let's keep that canary for 30m and collect flame samples + kv metrics. If stable, we can promote and then iterate on batch heuristics + prefix-merge.

samir: I'll follow up with a short perf-run that toggles batch_bias param to nudge kernel selector toward 8-12 request minibatches for small-seq traffic. Quick experiment config:
```json
{"workload":"small-chat","batch_bias":1.2,"minibatch_target":10}
```

alicia: I'll draft the KV prefix-merge and add unit tests for cache key normalization.

jon: Recording actions:
- samir: run batch-bias experiments and post results (ETA 3h)
- alicia: PR for prefix-merge heuristic (ETA 4h)
- maya: watch canary and collect traces (ETA 30m)
- ryan: stand by to rollback if p95 regresses

maya: thanks all — good turnout. Filing a short incident note and linking to this thread for postmortem if we promote. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Canary metrics snapshot uploaded: https://metrics.internal/redwood/canary/6489990000

samir: preliminary conclusion: main surface was host-side small-write churn + cache fragmentation. Coalescing + kernel hint revert buys immediate wins; batching & cache heuristics will be next wave.

maya: Closing loop later with numbers. If anyone sees other anomalies ping here.
